items.basis: The proposed adhesion-based mechanism is not a direct solution to the rotor imbalance vibration problem, as it only addresses the sample-layer disturbance caused by the imbalance, not the imbalance itself. This is evident from the provided evidence [doi:10.1177/1077546304035603], which discusses dynamic balancing of a centrifuge, but does not mention adhesion forces as a solution.

The candidate fails to consider the boundary condition of the rotor's material properties and its interaction with the adhesion forces. The provided evidence [doi:10.1016/0022-460x(82)90319-4] discusses non-linear effects in high-speed rotor noise, but does not provide any information on how the rotor's material properties would affect the adhesion forces.

The evidence [doi:10.1002/cpz1.70454] discusses a bacterial lysis observation over time assay (BLOTS) for high-throughput isolation, sequencing, and characterization, which is unrelated to the problem of rotor imbalance vibration. This evidence contradicts the claim that the adhesion-based mechanism would improve centrifuge performance.

The candidate fails to demonstrate that the adhesion-based mechanism would provide any significant improvement over the baseline, as the predicted effect of reducing vibration displacement to below 20 micrometers is not a substantial improvement over the baseline. The provided evidence [doi:10.1016/j.ohx.2025.e00694] discusses a centrifugal device for dust adhesion measurement, but does not provide any information on how this device would improve centrifuge performance.

The candidate fails to provide any information on how the adhesion-based mechanism would be implemented in practice, such as how the adhesion forces would be generated and controlled. The provided evidence [doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0326938] discusses LEGO as a versatile platform for building reconfigurable low-cost lab equipment, but does not provide any information on how this platform would be used to implement the adhesion-based mechanism.

The candidate fails to provide any information on how the vibration displacement would be measured accurately, as the provided evidence [doi:10.1177/1077546304035603] discusses dynamic balancing of a centrifuge, but does not provide any information on measurement techniques.
